item.title: Supplementary Drawback Claim Within 3 Months Limitation of AEPC Valuation: CESTAT Sets Aside Customs Rejection Order [Read Order]
item.description: The Bench noted that No delay could be Attributed to Appellant as they Consistently Engaged with Authorities and took swift Action

item.title: Defective DIR‑12 Cannot Remove Directors: Calcutta HC Orders ROC to Reconsider After Hearing All Parties [Read Order]
item.description: Since the ROC had already taken the position that the DIR‑12 was defective and invalid, the Court held that the proper course was for the ROC to adjudicate both objections together after granting a fair hearing.

item.title: Vesting of Assets in Official Liquidator Post‑Winding‑Up No Basis to Quash Criminal Case against Petitioner: Calcutta HC [Read Order]
item.description: The court underscored the narrow scope of inherent powers under Section 482 CrPC. The Court reiterated that quashing is permissible only when allegations, even if taken at face value, fail to disclose any cognizable offence.

item.title: AC‑DC & DC‑DC Power Modules Qualify as Static Converters: CAAR Grants Nil BCD Benefit for Telecom Equipment in Favour of Sanmina SCI [Read Order]
item.description: CAAR concluded that the modules possess the essential character of static converters and therefore fall within the tariff entry covering such devices. Based on this classification, the Authority extended the benefit of nil BCD applicable to static converters used in telecom equipment.

item.title: GST Authorities cannot Seize Cash as ‘Goods’ under CGST Act: Calcutta HC Orders De-Sealing of ₹24 Lakh [Read Order]
item.description: The High Court held that GST authorities cannot seize or seal cash under the CGST Act and ordered de-sealing of Rs. 24 lakh seized during search proceedings

item.title: Capital Gains for Home Buyers: Section 54F vs. Section 86 Explained [Old vs New Tax Act Series- Article 1]
item.description: This Article details the legal shift on capital gains on transfer of certain capital assets not to be charged in case of investment in residential houses.

item.title: Rough Estimates in Private Diaries Not Sufficient to Prove Clandestine Clearance: CESTAT Sets Aside Central Excise Duty Demand and Penalties [Read Order]
item.description: The Tribunal reinforced settled legal position that allegations of clandestine clearance must be backed by cogent, positive, and tangible evidence

item.title: Income Tax Dept. cannot Deny STCL Set-off against LTCG after accepting Same Claim in Factually-Identical Connected Cases: Bombay HC [Read Judgment]
item.description: The High Court shunned the Revenue’s contradictory stand noting that the set-off had been permitted in the case of the assessee’s brother and father

item.title: Small-Scale Exemption Cannot be Denied without Evidence: CESTAT Rules Expert Opinion Inadmissible, Sets Aside Excise Duty Demand [Read Order]
item.description: Small-Scale Exemption Cannot be Denied without Evidence: CESTAT Rules Expert Opinion Inadmissible, Sets Aside Excise Duty Demand [Read Order]

item.title: GST Portal Glitches Blocking TRAN‑1 Filing cannot Defeat Transitional ITC Claim: Delhi HC Orders ₹99 Lakh Credit to be Reflected in ECL [Read Order]
item.description: Relying on precedents such as Siemens Ltd. (Bombay HC), Vision Distribution (Delhi HC), and Dell International (Madras HC), the Court ruled that legitimate credit reflected in TRAN‑1 must be carried forward.
